_note: Placement map for room 15 (Rios Room), second floor, level 2 -- ROUND 2. The footprint was re-traced under round 1 (was 15.5 x 16, now 12.5 x 11.7) and the ORIENTATION changed with it, so every piece was re-authored, not just moved. Reference photos: docs/photos-jpg/'Rios room.jpg' (primary) + 'Rios Room 1/2/3.jpg'. As in round 1, every piece is AUTHORED IN ROOM-LOCAL COORDINATES and placed with rot=0 and pos = (bbox centre x, bbox min y, bbox centre z) -- exactly the seat the app gives a model. Build scripts: scratchpad/build15r2/{common,shell,furniture,floor,openings}.py -- re-run any of them from that directory with backend/.venv/Scripts/python.exe and the piece is rebuilt and re-placed idempotently by name. scratchpad/build15/ is round 1 and is superseded.

_room.name: Rios Room
_room.orientation_note: ROUND 1 HAD THIS 180 DEGREES OUT. Re-derived from docs/floor plan/'Second Floor Plan App.png' plus the level-2 world rects: in that plan, up = world +z and right = world -x (fixed by two adjacencies -- room 25 'Room 7' is the Closet drawn below Rios Room and is at world z 17.3..22.7 i.e. NORTH of it; 'Second floor bathroom' is drawn left of Rios Room and is room 26 at world x 10.5..18.6 i.e. EAST of it). The plan draws the two windows on its top wall, which is therefore the WORLD SOUTH wall. So: SOUTH (z=11.7) is the exterior wall with both windows, the ladder shelf between them and a rubber plant at each end. NORTH (z=0) has the closet double door at the WEST end (room 25 sits behind exactly that span, local x 0.1..8.7) and the entry door at the east end. WEST (x=0) is exterior and carries the birdcage, tucked into the SW corner. EAST (x=12.5) carries the console, the landscape art, the tower fan, the drum-shade lamp and the trailing plant. Photo check: the primary photo is shot from the entry door looking SOUTH, so its screen-left is EAST (console, wide window) and its screen-right is WEST (cage, narrow window, plant).

_camera.note: World coordinates, for `roomkit.shot --pose-json ... --level 2 --day`. Eye is local (10.3, 0.15) at 5.2 ft -- standing in the entry doorway looking SSW, the primary photo's vantage. The photo itself is taken from OUTSIDE the doorway with the door leaf framing the shot; a camera at world z < 22.7 renders a flat grey screen (something in the void north of the room fills the frame), so the pose stands just inside instead. Cost: the snake plant and the gallery art, which live on the north wall either side of the camera, are out of frame -- see the north pose.
_camera.doll_note: Use doll_nw, NOT the `doll` pose roomkit.rooms prints. Walls are FrontSide with inward normals, so the two walls nearest the camera are culled: from the south-east (the generated `doll`) that culls the window wall and the console wall and leaves the two least interesting sides, and the window units -- which are objects, never culled -- hang in mid-air where their wall used to be. From the north-west the culled pair is north+east, so the shot looks straight into the windows and the console.

_surfaces.note: Set with PATCH /api/house/room/15. No wall wash: round 1's room-filling emissive box is deleted and daylight.js's fix is left to do the work. Metered after the rebuild, room 15's four walls read 236/204/174/147 against an EMPTY room 13 (same floor, near-identical size) at 238/211/182/158 -- i.e. this room is no longer compensating for the renderer. The sun in `--day` is at azimuth 155, so the SOUTH window wall is always the darkest surface; the photo is backlit and agrees.

_openings.note: TWO REAL CUT OPENINGS in the south wall (edge_index 2, whose offset is measured WEST from x=W). East: offset 1.55, width 2.70. West: offset 7.75, width 2.20. Both elevation 1.75, height 4.85. Type is `passage`, not `window`: a `window` opening gets the app's own 0.3 ft deep pale-blue glass box centred on the wall, which would sit 1.8 in proud of the blinds and lay a blue film over the unit -- the exact cast the critic flagged on round 1's fake glass. `passage` cuts the hole and draws nothing, and the window GLB brings its own pane, blinds, stool and casing. The two doors are NOT cut: room 25 is behind the closet doors but there is no room at all behind the entry door (world x 6.7..10.5, z 17.3..22.7 is unassigned), so a real opening there would show void. Both are closed leaves flush on the wall, which is correct from the only viewpoint judged.

Rios Ceiling.note: Flat 12.5 x 11.7 plane at y=7.99, ONE-SIDED facing down so it is solid at eye level and invisible from above (check with a plan pose -- you must still see the floor). A downward plane collects almost no light here, so its white is emissive-driven (#ffffff albedo + #bcbcbc emissive), tuned so the ceiling metres ~217 against ~155 walls: critic item 10 was that the two rendered at the same value. Four cans at local (3.3,3.2) (9.1,3.2) (3.3,8.3) (9.1,8.3), each now a TRIM RING + a recessed reveal + a hot lens (emissive_strength 7) rather than round 1's flat white ellipse (critic item 9). Smoke detector (6.1,6.05) and the HVAC register (5.9,1.35) are there too. All fixtures are downward-facing discs/rects, never cylinders: a cylinder's top cap is front-facing from above and leaves white dots lying on the floor in plan view. Vertical separation between the ceiling plane and each fixture was raised to 0.02-0.09 ft after two cans z-fought into crescents at 0.004.

Rios Floor.note: THREE critic items live in this one piece. (4) Planks are 0.583 ft = 7 in, not round 1's 0.52-with-12-columns-across-15.5-ft which read as 15 in, and the eight tones sit inside a 10-level band. (4 again) Tone is calibrated against the RENDER, not picked off the photo -- the app renders an authored sRGB value about 1.35x brighter, so #4f4d4a lands at ~133, matching the photo's 125 near the camera; round 1's palette was tuned before the daylight.js fix and is now far too dark. (3a) The window light pool: two smooth 2-D falloffs from the south-wall openings, quantised to 13 tones with a per-cell dither so the pool's edge breaks up. The FIRST attempt used stacked rectangles and its outermost band drew a hard straight line across the floor -- the same failure the wall wash was killed for; do not go back to bands. Pool cells are one plank column wide and inset by the joint so the seams still show through. (3b) Contact shadows: nine nested superellipse blobs under every piece that meets the floor, keyed to the pool tone underneath so a shadow inside the pool does not halo. Blobs are CLAMPED to the room rect -- the app seats a model by its bbox centre, so a shadow hanging over the wall shifts the whole plank field sideways. Layers: slab 0.010 | planks 0.014 | pool 0.0165.. | shadows 0.023..

Rios Baseboards.note: White 5.5 in x 0.9 in skirting on all four walls with a 0.055 ft chamfer cap, gapped at both north-wall door casings (local x 1.12..6.68 and 8.62..11.88).

Rios Window East.note: THE headline fix (critic item 1). Round 1 built 4.69 and 3.74 ft wide x 6.15 ft TALL with sill 1.40 and head 7.55 -- a 5-inch header in an 8 ft room, so they read as French doors and crushed the apparent ceiling. Measured off the photo the glass is ~4.8 ft tall over a ~1.7 ft sill under a ~1.3 ft header, and the floor plan gives the wide unit as 3.31 ft of wall. So: opening local x 8.25..10.95 (2.70), sill 1.75, head 6.60, casing out to 7.95..11.25, head cap topping out at 7.00, leaving 1.0 ft of header. Sits over a real cut opening. The pane behind the blinds is emissive WHITE with a low foliage mass, not round 1's pale-green scalloped panel -- critic item 7 was that the panel gave the whole wall a green cast; the photo is blown-out daylight through white slats. Blinds are lowered with the slats open at 28 deg.

Rios Window West.note: Same unit, narrower: opening local x 2.55..4.75 (2.20). The photo's two windows differ in width by roughly 5:4 and the plan agrees.

Rios Door.note: The entry door, NORTH wall, opening local x 8.90..11.60 -- 2.70 x 6.75, a standard single door, against round 1's 3.60 x 7.10 (critic item 12). Six-panel white leaf with a #cfccc6 reveal behind each raised panel: on a flat white leaf under this renderer the panels have no shading at all and the door reads as a blank slab. Black lever. Built CLOSED (see _openings).

Rios Closet Doors.note: White double closet door at the WEST end of the north wall, opening local x 1.40..6.40 -- room 25 ('Room 7', 8.6 x 5.4, labelled 'Closet' on the floor plan) sits directly behind that span.

Rios Ladder Shelf.note: White leaning A-frame ladder shelf standing BETWEEN the two windows on the 2.9 ft pier, feet at z 10.35, top rail against the wall at z 11.56. Five shelves at y 0.52 / 1.85 / 3.06 / 4.20 / 5.30. Bottom shelf holds the two WHITE fabric bins the photo shows; everything above was repalletted to muted greys/soft greens with a couple of teal accents, because critic item 11 was that round 1's candy-coloured blocks made the loudest colour in the render the one thing not in the room. A shadow strip is baked under each shelf front -- the app renders no shadows and a white ladder on a white wall is otherwise invisible.

Rios Round Art.note: White-framed square canvas with the dark circular line motif, hung on the pier so its lower half sits behind the ladder's top two shelves -- the overlap the photo shows. Shrunk from 2.30 x 2.15 to fit between the two window head casings.

Rios Pouf Grey.note: Cream chunky-knit round pouf under the EAST (wide) window.

Rios Pouf Teal.note: The teal knit pouf, west of the ladder shelf under the west window.

Rios Rubber Plant.note: The rubber tree at the WEST end of the window wall, white pot on a splayed four-leg black stand at local (2.65, 10.95), canopy drifting EAST over the west window -- which is what the photo shows. Critic item 2 was that round 1's plant intersected the window aperture, the birdcage footprint and 0.09 ft of wall: the canopy is now 25% smaller with a shorter reach, its farthest leaf sits 0.2 ft clear of the wall plane, and the cage was pulled south past it. Leaves are tilted 48-76 deg toward vertical -- authored flat (the leaf primitive is a horizontal disc) they are edge-on from eye level and the plant reads as a totem pole.

Rios Rubber Plant East.note: NEW in round 2. There are TWO rubber trees in this room, one at each end of the window wall -- 'Rios Room 2.jpg' shows one in the SE corner arching over the console wall, and the primary photo shows its leaves cropped at the extreme left edge. Round 1 read the two as one plant and that is most of why its corner never resolved. Pot at local (11.72, 10.55), canopy drifting NORTH along the east wall.

Rios Birdcage.note: The large parrot cage on a rolling stand, back against the WEST wall with its long side running north-south (x 0.12..2.02, z 7.40..10.60). Critic item 6 was that round 1 stood it 1.3 ft off the wall, ran it 4.6 ft into the room and built it ~5.9 ft tall where the photo measures 4.5-5 and tucks it hard into the corner: it is now 4.95 ft to the top of the barrel arch (stand 1.40, mesh body to 4.10) and its south end is 1.1 ft off the window wall, which is the closest it gets without eating the rubber plant's stand. The cage door outline moved to the EAST face -- the one you actually see from the room.

Rios Console.note: Narrow white console against the EAST wall (photos 2 and 3), 4.0 long x 1.15 deep x 2.55 high with a lower shelf: six shoes on the shelf, four small potted plants and a dark tray on top.

Rios Landscape Art.note: The muted gold/grey abstract landscape hung over the console.

Rios Tower Fan.note: The white cylindrical tower fan at the north end of the console run.

Rios Lamp Drum.note: NEW in round 2 (critic item 8): the bronze drum-shade floor lamp that frames the left of the primary photo, standing on the east wall between the doorway and the console. Nickel disc base and stem, 0.98 ft drum shade with a lit underside. NOT called anything with 'floor' in it -- objects.js makes any object whose name matches floor|ceiling|wall wash|baseboards|crown unpickable, and this is real furniture.

Rios Trailing Plant.note: NEW in round 2 (critic item 8): the trailing plant hanging high on the EAST wall above the console -- photo 3's top-right corner, and the dark leaves at the top-left of the primary photo. Wall bracket, white pot, six vines dropping 1.1-2.5 ft.

Rios Snake Plant.note: Snake plant in a white pot on the NORTH wall between the closet doors and the entry door -- that is where photo 3 puts it, and it is the same plant that fills the near right foreground of the primary photo (which is shot from outside the door, so the plant is beside the lens).

Rios Gallery Art.note: The small framed print on the north wall between the closet and the entry door, above the snake plant (photo 3).

_gaps: The judged pose stands just inside the doorway, not outside it like the photo, because a camera north of z=22.7 renders a flat grey frame. Cost: the snake plant and the gallery art (north wall, either side of the lens) and the door leaf/casing that frame the real photo are not in the judged shot. Use the `north` pose for those.

The south wall is the darkest surface in the room (metered 147 against 236 on the north) because roomkit's --day sun is at azimuth 155 and the app renders no bounce. The photo is backlit and agrees in direction, but the photo's window wall varies from 86 to 165 across its width while ours is flat. Nothing is faking it -- see _surfaces.
Round 1's 'Rios Wall Wash' is DELETED. Do not rebuild it; daylight.js was fixed app-wide and room 15 now metres within a few points of an empty room on the same floor.
The two rubber trees, the ladder-shelf clutter, the cage toys and the console shoes are colour-blocked stand-ins, not modelled objects -- they read at room scale and fall apart in a close-up.
'Rios Floor' covers the whole slab, so it is named to stay unpickable (objects.js SURFACE_RE); check_pick reports 43/49 floor samples still resolve to the room.
The window pane is emissive, not a light: the daylight coming 'through' the openings does not illuminate anything. The floor light pool is baked into the plank field to stand in for it.

The entry door has no room behind it in the layout (world x 6.7..10.5, z 17.3..22.7 is unassigned void between room 15 and hallway 17), so it is a closed leaf rather than a cut opening. If that void is ever traced as a landing, cut a real `door` opening there.
